_comment: Shared shortcode-structure parity corpus — the SINGLE source of truth for
what block structure each markdown input has. Consumed by TWO enforced gates:
• TS    packages/moss-syntax/src/__tests__/shortcode-corpus.test.ts  (the shared text scanner, scanShortcodeBlocks; the Lezer grammar is tied to it by scan.test.ts's cross-check)
Both must match this corpus, so the editor live-view parse can never drift from
the build without a red test. Structural facts only (names + nesting + grid cell
counts) — language-neutral, no byte offsets. `gridCells` is asserted for grid
blocks only (buttons store items, not cells, on the build side). Only the
typed shortcodes are listed: a closed block with any other name (an unknown
name, a nameless {.class} region) is a wrapper whose contents are not listed,
and an unclosed opener is plain text, so what it holds is listed as if it were
not there. A `+++` inside a nested block divides that block, not the grid.

cases.name: grid, no divider → one cell
grid 2, one +++ → two cells
grid 1:1:2, two +++ → three cells
top-level buttons (no children, not a grid)
nested ::::buttons inside :::grid (the leak bug)
Homepage shape: grid 2, nested buttons in cell 1, +++ at grid level
two top-level blocks in order
hero (no cells, no children)
gallery (no cells, no children)
same-length nesting: a bare closer closes the innermost block
mixed lengths nest the same as equal ones
three levels, every closer is three colons
a closer of another length still closes
a name starting with a digit opens a nested block
a non-ASCII name opens a nested block
a nameless attribute fence opens a nested block
a stray closer after a closed block is ignored
an unclosed opener is plain text
an unclosed outer leaves the inner block it shares a closer with
colons followed by a plain word are body text, not a closer
